subject: Numeracy
title: How many? Counting with care
subtopics: The last number tells how many
objectives: Children will count up to five objects without skipping any.
Children will check a count by counting again.
content: Counting up to five objects without skipping or repeating any, answering how many with the last number and checking the count.
teachingActivities: Show how to move counted objects to a "done" tray; model a mistake and fix it; praise careful touching rather than speed.
learnerActivities: Count scattered and lined-up objects, check by counting again, find mistakes and say how many.
resources: A teddy puppet who makes counting mistakes
assessment: Check one-to-one touching, order of number words and whether the child says how many with the last number.
expectedOutcomes: Counts to three reliably and to five with growing accuracy.
Says the last number as the answer to how many.

lessons.title: Count without missing any
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will count up to five objects by moving each one from a "to count" tray to a "done" tray.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to three reliably and to five with support, and add one more to a small group.
resources: Two trays labelled to count and done
lessons.starter: Spread five blocks on the mat and say "Let me count them. I must not miss any!" Count while pointing quickly and miss one. Say "Oh no, I missed one!"
teacherActivities: Show the "to count" tray and the "done" tray. Move one block at a time, saying the number.
Say "When all the blocks are in the done tray, the last number tells how many."
Let a child move the blocks while the group counts.
Try with three blocks and then four.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say the numbers with you.
Children say "five" when the last block is moved.
Child moves each block and the group counts.
Children count each group carefully.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the "to count" tray and the "done" tray. Move one block at a time, saying the number. Children: Children watch and say the numbers with you.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "When all the blocks are in the done tray, the last number tells how many." Children: Children say "five" when the last block is moved.
Step 3. Teacher: Let a child move the blocks while the group counts. Children: Child moves each block and the group counts.
Step 4. Teacher: Try with three blocks and then four. Children: Children count each group carefully.

practical.title: To count and done
steps: Give each pair two trays and up to five blocks.
Move each block from one tray to the other while saying the numbers.
Say the last number as the answer.
practical.safety: Use blocks larger than a child’s fist; keep trays on the floor; supervise group play.

differentiation.support: Count three blocks and move each one hand-over-hand.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count five blocks without the trays by pointing.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many blocks did you count?
questions.expected: The correct number, up to five.

expectedOutcomes: Says the last number as the answer
lessons.conclusion: Put all the blocks back and say "Careful counting, well done."
lessons.homeConnection: Count spoons or shoes at home by moving each one aside as you count.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "count up to five objects by moving each one from a "to count" tray to a "done" tray" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Touch one, move one, say the number. Touch two, move two, count with me.

lessons.title: Teddy makes a mistake
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will help Teddy find and fix counting mistakes.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to three reliably and to five with support, and add one more to a small group.
lessons.starter: Hold the teddy puppet and say "Teddy is learning to count but he makes mistakes. Can you help him?"
teacherActivities: Teddy counts four fruits but says "one, two, four". Ask "Is that right?"
Ask "What number did Teddy forget?" and count again together.
Teddy touches one fruit twice. Ask children to spot the mistake.
Let a child be the teacher and show Teddy how to count.
learnerActivities: Children shake their heads and say "no".
Children say "three" and count correctly.
Children point to the fruit counted twice.
Child counts and the group checks.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Teddy counts four fruits but says "one, two, four". Ask "Is that right?" Children: Children shake their heads and say "no".
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "What number did Teddy forget?" and count again together. Children: Children say "three" and count correctly.
Step 3. Teacher: Teddy touches one fruit twice. Ask children to spot the mistake. Children: Children point to the fruit counted twice.
Step 4. Teacher: Let a child be the teacher and show Teddy how to count. Children: Child counts and the group checks.

practical.title: Help Teddy count
steps: Give each pair a teddy and a tray of fruits.
One child makes the teddy count with a mistake.
The partner spots and fixes it.
practical.safety: Use toy fruits larger than a fist; keep the tray on the table; supervise play.

differentiation.support: Let the teddy make only one mistake, such as forgetting a number.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to give the teddy a hint to count correctly.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How can we help Teddy?
questions.expected: Count again slowly and touch each one.

lessons.conclusion: Thank Teddy for learning and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Count a set of objects at home and check by counting again.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "help Teddy find and fix counting mistakes" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Scattered or in a line?
lessons.subject: Numeracy
lessons.subtopic: The last number tells how many
objectives: Children will count the same objects when they are scattered and when they are in a line and see the number stays the same.
successCriteria: Says the same number for a line
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to three reliably and to five with support, and add one more to a small group.
lessons.starter: Spread five blocks randomly on the mat and ask "How many?" Count them together. Then line them up and ask "How many now? Did the number change?"
teacherActivities: Count the blocks while they are scattered. Say "Five."
Line them up and count again. Say "Still five."
Spread them out wide and count again. Ask "Is it still five?"
Let each child spread and line up the blocks and count them.
learnerActivities: Children touch and count to five.
Children count the line and say "five".
Children count and say "still five".
Child rearranges the blocks and counts to five.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Count the blocks while they are scattered. Say "Five." Children: Children touch and count to five.
Step 2. Teacher: Line them up and count again. Say "Still five." Children: Children count the line and say "five".
Step 3. Teacher: Spread them out wide and count again. Ask "Is it still five?" Children: Children count and say "still five".
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child spread and line up the blocks and count them. Children: Child rearranges the blocks and counts to five.

practical.title: Scatter and line
steps: Scatter them, count, line them up, count again.
practical.safety: Use large blocks; keep them on the mat; supervise.

differentiation.support: Use three blocks and count them together before and after.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count seven objects with help and say how many.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Knows the number stays the same
lessons.conclusion: Put the blocks in the basket together saying the numbers.
lessons.homeConnection: Count the same objects in different arrangements and see if the number changes.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "count the same objects when they are scattered and when they are in a line and see the number stays the same" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Count the class
lessons.subject: Numeracy
lessons.subtopic: The last number tells how many
objectives: Children will count friends, chairs and shoes in the room.
successCriteria: Counts people or objects in the room
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to three reliably and to five with support, and add one more to a small group.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we count real things in our classroom. How many chairs? How many friends are sitting?"
teacherActivities: Count the chairs together and move each one to the side as you count.
Count the children sitting in a circle by tapping each shoulder.
Count the shoes in a pile by pairing them.
Ask "Are there more chairs or more children?"
learnerActivities: Children count each chair.
Children count each friend.
Children count the shoes and say how many.
Children compare and say "more".
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Count the chairs together and move each one to the side as you count. Children: Children count each chair.
Step 2. Teacher: Count the children sitting in a circle by tapping each shoulder. Children: Children count each friend.
Step 3. Teacher: Count the shoes in a pile by pairing them. Children: Children count the shoes and say how many.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "Are there more chairs or more children?" Children: Children compare and say "more".

practical.title: Classroom counting
steps: Count chairs, friends and shoes in the room.
practical.safety: Keep walkways clear; children count calmly; no pushing.

differentiation.support: Count only up to three with an adult.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count items outdoors, such as leaves or stones too large to swallow.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many chairs?
questions.expected: The number of chairs, up to five.

questions.question: Are there more chairs or friends?

expectedOutcomes: Counts real things in the room
lessons.conclusion: Count the whole class together and clap.
lessons.homeConnection: Count people at the table or shoes at the door.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "count friends, chairs and shoes in the room" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Careful counting stations
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will show they can count up to five carefully at three stations.
successCriteria: Counts up to five without skipping
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to three reliably and to five with support, and add one more to a small group.
resources: Station 1: to count and done trays
lessons.starter: Sing the counting song and show the three stations.
teacherActivities: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely.
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children play at each station.
Child counts and checks.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely. Children: Children play at each station.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "How many?" and "Can you check?" Children: Child counts and checks.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Station circuit
practical.safety: Use large items only; supervise stations; keep floors clear.

differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to count objects for a friend.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: counts to three reliably and to five with growing accuracy; says how many with the last number; checks by counting again.

questions.question: How many are there?
questions.expected: The correct number up to five.

questions.question: Can you count again to check?
questions.expected: Child recounts and gets the same.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 7
lessons.conclusion: Sing the counting song and tidy up together.
lessons.homeConnection: Count things carefully at home this week.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "show they can count up to five carefully at three stations" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
